summary.headline: Apollo Micro Systems posted record Q4 FY26 revenue of INR293 crores (+81% YoY) and FY26 PAT margin of 16% standalone, with order book at INR1,432 crores.
summary.overview: Consolidated Q4 FY26 was the company's highest ever quarter: revenue INR293 crores (+81% YoY), EBITDA INR68 crores (+88%), and PAT INR37 crores (+164%). For FY26, consolidated revenue rose 61% to INR904 crores, EBITDA excluding other income rose 69% to INR218 crores, and PAT rose 91% to INR107 crores. Management said standalone FY26 revenue growth was about 36%, below the earlier 45-50% organic CAGR guidance, which it attributed to customer approvals delaying Q4 execution. The call stressed Vision 2036, new land-systems entry, export pipeline, and new licences, while giving little numerical guidance on IDL Explosives or order inflows.

segments.name: IDL Explosives (subsidiary)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue around INR380 crores, described as roughly flat expectation going forward; company has been loss-making with negative EBITDA and is in a transformation phase, with revenue and margin guidance promised from Q3 FY27 onwards.

segments.name: Standalone / group
segments.commentary: Standalone FY26 revenue growth about 36% vs prior 45-50% organic CAGR guidance; standalone PAT margin 16% vs internal target of 15%.

segments.name: Air, land and sea platforms
segments.commentary: Heritage in air and underwater (missiles, EW, avionics, torpedoes, sonars, mines); land systems entry planned in FY26-27 with trials scheduled in upcoming quarters. No revenue split given.

guidance_outlook: Management expects large-ticket orders to arrive during FY27 and the order book to increase significantly on both standalone and consolidated basis; no quantified inflow number given.
Company expects to grow at a similar rate in FY27 and FY28, no formal revenue or margin guidance for FY27 given.
IDL Explosives revenue and margin guidance to be provided from Q3 FY27; currently undergoing transformation.
Explosives expansion: TNT (500 tonnes) and HMX (50 tonnes) licences obtained for industrial use; DPRs for larger defence explosive capacity being prepared.
Vision 2036 to be unveiled soon; no financial parameters given on the call.
Management said a further acquisition by subsidiary Apollo Defence Industries is expected to close before end of FY27 (Q1 FY27 timeframe), details under NDA.
capex_capacity: Unit 3 (Hardware Park, Telangana): phase one civil work complete; phase two civil work ongoing; MEP and facade works underway in phase one; machinery from Unit 1 to be shifted in stages.
Company is setting up in-house test facilities previously outsourced, expected to improve inventory holding days over coming quarters.
Specialised RF seeker testing facility planned at upcoming Hardware Park unit.
Greenfield expansion in Telangana referenced as an FY26 milestone; capacity needed for export orders to be ready before commitments.
demand_pricing: Order book INR1,432 crores at 31 March 2026 consolidated; management declined to give composition and said conversion depends on approvals, with some orders spilling into FY28.
Q4 FY26 revenue growth attributed to execution of order book and transition of multiple products into production; most business to date is development orders, production orders expected in FY27-28.
Standalone growth shortfall due to customer approvals pending for projects that had been expected in Q4 FY26.
Mines: two variants of shallow and deep water and two types (limpet and diver-carried) cited as an immediate market of roughly INR4,000-4,500 crores; some orders expected this year, others later.
DAC approval for a large Navy order (mines/torpedoes) said to be expected imminently; no value given.
Export offers submitted; first export order received in FY26; no export revenue quantified.

qa_highlights.question: What order inflows are expected in FY27-28 to sustain revenue growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects large-ticket orders anytime in FY27 and a significant rise in order book on both standalone and consolidated bases; no quantum given.

qa_highlights.question: What are the key tenets and financial parameters of the FY36 Vision?
qa_highlights.answer: Four pillars: global OEM, diversified land/air/sea revenue, Indian and export expansion, and R&D-led innovation; numbers to be shared later.

qa_highlights.question: What is IDL's revenue, utilisation and margin profile?
qa_highlights.answer: IDL did around INR380 crores in FY26 and is loss-making, with operating losses reduced; revenue and margin guidance to come from Q3 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Why a smaller TNT and HMX expansion, and what capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Current licences (500 t TNT, 50 t HMX) are for industrial explosives; larger defence-capacity expansion is at DPR stage and will be disclosed later.

qa_highlights.question: Why was FY26 standalone growth below 45-50% guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Some projects planned for Q4 FY26 were delayed by pending customer approvals; management expects to catch up and maintain momentum.

qa_highlights.question: Will the order book be executed in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Some orders will execute in FY27 and others will spill over; management said revenue growth will continue at a similar pace, no numeric estimate.

risks_watch: Order inflow visibility: the company has not quantified FY27 inflows and says order composition will not be disclosed.
IDL Explosives remains loss-making; consolidated margins could be diluted until transformation shows results (guidance deferred to Q3 FY27).
Revenue timing risk from customer approvals and DAC clearances; Q4 FY26 slippage shows standalone growth can fall short of guidance.
Promoter pledge still around 39% per an analyst; management declined to give a roadmap beyond FY27.
Working capital and inventory: 359-day cycle and rising inventory and receivables, with holding days expected to improve only as production orders and in-house test facilities come in.
Pending acquisition by Apollo Defence Industries under NDA; funding not disclosed.
summary.management_tone: Confident and promotional on long-term vision and licences, but evasive on quantitative detail: declined to give order composition, IDL guidance, FY36 financials, and FY27 margin/revenue targets. Acknowledged the standalone growth shortfall versus prior guidance, attributing it to customer approvals.
key_quotes: We do make mistakes. Some bets will succeed, while others may require a course correction.
As and when these production orders keep hitting, and then the revenue starts recognizing, I think the inventory levels will slowly come down.
